title: Two synapse detectors gave a median 94.7 percent input overlap in 27 selected fly visual types
abstract: We compared two synapse detectors in one FlyWire v783 specimen using fixed cell labels and a public flicker activity sample. Five of 32 activity type names had no exact match and were excluded before fitting. The 27 retained types had a median common normalized input fraction of 94.69 percent. The nearest input-profile neighbor agreed for 25 types, and pair-distance rank correlation was 0.9791. Nested prediction with target flies excluded reduced mean shape error by 16.59 percent for Buhmann and 18.54 percent for Princeton in type holdout. Family holdout gave smaller point reductions of 4.57 and 6.18 percent. Paired fixed-prediction resampling ranges included zero for the detector error difference. An independent calculation checked all 108 outer predictions. The study shows technical agreement for a selected input-profile model, not detector accuracy or biological transfer. One specimen, shared segmentation, current labels, type averaging, and reused calcium trial means limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval steps are included. Noncommercial source tables and derived record-level materials remain external.
